newsitem.title: TURKEY: Pakistan's Sharif says worried over India missiles.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan's Sharif says worried over India missiles.

text.p: Pakistan's Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif said at a summit of Moslem nations in Istanbul on Sunday that he was deeply concerned about the deployment by India of missiles along the border with Pakistan.
"As we pursue peace with India, we are deeply concerned that India has deployed short-range missiles, the Prithvis, along the border with Pakistan," Sharif said.
Sharif, in a speech to the Developing-Eight (D-8) summit, said Pakistan was determined to sustain a dialogue with India.
"While Pakistan does not wish to embark on a ballistic missile race in south Asia which the region can ill-afford, it cannot remain indifferent to its legitimate security concerns," Sharif said.

Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral has denied a U.S. newspaper report of the deployment of the Prithvis, which Islamabad says pose a threat that Pakistan will take the "necessary measures" to meet.
The Washington Post two weeks ago quoted U.S. intelligence agencies as saying India had moved up less than a dozen Prithvis to near Jullundur in the northeast state of Punjab.
There have been repeated reports, which Islamabad denies, that Pakistan has obtained M-11 missiles from China.
India and Pakistan have fought three wars since their independence in 1947, two of them over Kashmir. India rules two-thirds of Kashmir and Pakistan the rest.
India accuses Pakistan of arming and training Moslem rebels fighting New Delhi's rule in Kashmir, while Islamabad says it provides them only moral and diplomatic support.
Pakistan says Kashmir is the core issue that the neighbours must resolve, while India says it is keen to make progress in other areas such as trade.
